questions.topic: Page 3: 1.3 THE 2-D CARTESIAN COORDINATE SYSTEM (Pages 3-4 Focus)
questions.questionText: Any point lying on the x-axis has a y-coordinate of 0.
questions.explanationAnswer: By definition, the x-axis is the line where the vertical distance (y-coordinate) from the origin is zero.
questions.explanationQuestion: The question tests the understanding of the properties of points on the x-axis.

questions.topic: Page 3: 1.3 THE 2-D CARTESIAN COORDINATE SYSTEM (Pages 3-4 Focus)
questions.questionText: Match the quadrant with the sign convention of its coordinates (x, y):
questions.explanationAnswer: Quadrant I is (+, +), Quadrant II is (-, +), Quadrant III is (-, -), and Quadrant IV is (+, -).
questions.explanationQuestion: The question requires matching quadrants to their respective coordinate sign patterns.

questions.topic: Page 3: 1.3 THE 2-D CARTESIAN COORDINATE SYSTEM (Pages 3-4 Focus)
questions.questionText: Given a point P(x, y), which of the following statements are correct regarding its coordinates?

options.optionText: x represents the perpendicular distance from the y-axis.
y represents the perpendicular distance from the x-axis.
x represents the perpendicular distance from the x-axis.
y represents the perpendicular distance from the y-axis.

multi: x represents the perpendicular distance from the y-axis.
y represents the perpendicular distance from the x-axis.
questions.explanationAnswer: The x-coordinate is the distance measured along the x-axis from the y-axis, and the y-coordinate is the distance measured along the y-axis from the x-axis.
questions.explanationQuestion: The question tests the definition of x and y coordinates as distances from the axes.
